title: Ideal Gas Law PVT Surface Explorer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive 3D PVT (Pressure-Volume-Temperature) surface explorer for an ideal gas (PV = nRT).

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (8, 6, 8) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation/zoom.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Background color: #1a1a2e (dark navy).
- Draw a 3D axis frame: X-axis = Volume (0 to 10 L), Y-axis = Pressure (0 to 10 atm), Z-axis = Temperature (0 to 1000 K). Label each axis with white text sprites at the ends.
- Render axis tick marks every 2 units on each axis.

## PVT Surface
- Generate a parametric mesh surface representing PV = nRT for n = 1 mol, R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K).
- Parameterize: for V in [0.5, 10] and T in [50, 1000], compute P = nRT/V. Clamp P to [0, 10].
- Use a grid of at least 50x50 vertices for smoothness.
- Color the surface using a gradient mapped to temperature: blue (cold, 50K) → red (hot, 1000K).
- Make the surface semi-transparent (opacity 0.7) with DoubleSide material.

## Probe Point
- Display a bright yellow sphere (radius 0.12) as a probe point that sits on the PVT surface.
- Initialize the probe at V=5, T=300 (compute P from ideal gas law: P = 1*0.0821*300/5 = 4.926 atm).
- The probe can be moved along the surface using keyboard controls.

## Isothermal and Isobaric Curves
- Draw an isothermal curve (constant T) through the current probe point as a bright cyan line (LineBasicMaterial, linewidth conceptual). This curve shows P vs V at the probe's current T.
- Draw an isobaric curve (constant P) through the current probe point as a bright magenta line. This curve shows T vs V at the probe's current P.
- Draw an isochoric curve (constant V) through the current probe point as a bright green line. This curve shows P vs T at the probe's current V.
- Update all three curves whenever the probe moves.

## User Interactions
- Arrow Left/Right: decrease/increase Volume by 0.25 (clamp to [0.5, 10]).
- Arrow Up/Down: increase/decrease Temperature by 25 K (clamp to [50, 1000]).
- Key 'I': toggle isothermal curve visibility.
- Key 'B': toggle isobaric curve visibility.
- Key 'V': toggle isochoric curve visibility.
- Key 'R': reset probe to initial position (V=5, T=300).
- Key 'N': cycle the moles value n through [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0] and regenerate the entire surface and update probe P accordingly.
- Key 'S': take a snapshot — store the current {P, V, T, n} into a snapshots array (max 5, FIFO).

## HUD / DOM Overlay
- Top-left panel (semi-transparent dark background, white text, monospace font) showing:
  - Current V, T, P values (P computed as nRT/V, displayed to 3 decimal places)
  - Current n value
  - Number of snapshots stored
  - Which curves are visible (ISO_T, ISO_P, ISO_V: ON/OFF)
- Bottom bar showing keyboard controls legend.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields, updated every frame:
  - probeV: current volume (number)
  - probeT: current temperature (number)
  - probeP: current pressure (number, computed as n*R*T/V)
  - n: current moles (number)
  - R: gas constant 0.0821 (number)
  - surfaceVertexCount: number of vertices in the surface mesh (number)
  - isothermalVisible: boolean
  - isobaricVisible: boolean
  - isochoricVisible: boolean
  - snapshots: array of {P, V, T, n} objects
  - snapshotCount: number of snapshots
  - probeWorldX: probe mesh world x position (number)
  - probeWorldY: probe mesh world y position (number)
  - probeWorldZ: probe mesh world z position (number)
  - idealGasError: absolute value of |PV - nRT| for current probe values (should be ~0)
  - cameraDistance: distance from camera to origin (number)
  - frameCount: incrementing frame counter (number)

## Physics Constraints
- The ideal gas law PV = nRT must hold at the probe point at all times. The idealGasError should be < 0.001.
- Pressure must always be positive and within [0, 10] atm display range.
- Volume must stay in [0.5, 10] L.
- Temperature must stay in [50, 1000] K.
- When n changes, P must update to maintain PV = nRT.
- Surface vertex positions must reflect the equation: y-coordinate proportional to P = nRT/V.
physics_constraints: PV = nRT must hold at probe point at all times (idealGasError < 0.001). P clamped to [0,10] atm, V clamped to [0.5,10] L, T clamped to [50,1000] K. Changing n regenerates surface and updates P = nRT/V. All displayed values must be self-consistent with the ideal gas law.
